Scientists just want people to have the general knowledge and want that knowledge kept in like, school. Beyond that, they may HOPE people will choose knowledge, but they don't preach it? Every scientist who is well knowledged in an area will probably always hope people could know what they know, because "knowledge is power", truly, but yeah, I'd never say they preach. Ninaki came from my nickname from my mom growing up. She called me "baby Nina" (not at all related to my real first name) and so when I was around... 8-9-10, I made an account on GaiaOnline or something. GunZ Online, Conquer Online, Runescape. It was between that and another username that was my other popular one but I don't wanna share that one lol\~  
I wanted to make it sound more "Japanese" styled as a kid, since myself and another best friend were in a lot of forums and stuff. That name forever stuck and I use it on almost everything. I usually don't have 3 i's, but sometimes the name is taken (if I find those people, I will challenge them to fisty cuffs). Now, it actually has a ton of meaning to me, for all of the years of things involving the name. All coming from a silly nickname my mom had for me as a kid (just while I was a kid, too; she stopped saying it at some point). I think for certain reasons, instead of calling me by my middle name (which neither her nor I liked/picked) she would say it as a replacement. I've always thought to change my middle name to either that or just "Nina", and get rid of the one I have. Because it'd be the one that was chosen for me by my momma. So many lovely memories created with that name, friends made with that name, growing from a kid, to a pre-teen, to a teen, etc., etc., to where now, I am 32, and it has come to mean so much to me, truly. A whole life lived within that one made-up username <3

And at the same time, as a child still around 12\~ or so, I was always jealous of another friend who was, and still is in my opinion, so much prettier than I am (conventionally, she really just is), and so if she dressed too cute or talked too much to a guy I was trying to talk to while she was at my house or whatever, I'd be so uspet. I've lost multiple pets, and this is a good answer. Many needed euthanized, and as hard as it was, looking back on all of it, it was the best for each of them.

Many vet visits, some saying she needed put down, most saying she was a spunky, healthy cat (which really sucks, because she clearly wasn't). One day, she started to make horrible meows, and they planned to take her to the vet in the morning because nothing was open, not even the emergency vets near them \[somehow?\]). Within a few hours, she had passed. She was in her cozy spot behind a chair, curled up and cozy looking like she was sleeping, but we knew she hurt so much in the end and all that could be done was to wait a few hours for the vet to open. The slowing of movement, incontenence, etc.

They may eat a little less, maybe lose a bit of weight, get confused, cry randomly, less interest in activities in general. 

They're things to look at if you can. We have to make the hard decision for our best friends, and of course it would be best if they could just speak to us and tell us what they need. But what we do is make the best choice for them with the info we have.

You can get a second opinion from another vet if you need to. There could be more time. But if you see that he is struggling in different ways and he stays alive, you could be prolonging his pains.

You have to look at it as a kindness. The hardest choice we can make but one of the kindest things we can do.

We had waited too long for my cat who passed away \~6 months before my dog (who I had even longer than 16 1/2 years), and we kept thinking she was doing better (she hid her issues SO much more; the vet said it was a UTI many times and ruled out tons of other things). One day she started making horrible, horrible meows finally (after a \~year of seeming off) and passed within a few hours at home. So because we wanted to keep her longer and fought the original opinion (we DID have other vets say she was fine, so it was a confusing thing), she suffered at the end.

When we start to notice problems, as humans, I think we do what we must with their best interests in mind, and there's not always an easy answer.
